meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'without' in everyday speech.
with a past-tense verb: я бы подумал = I would think
wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.text: Ты эти деньги через полгода вернёшь.

Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

Core Russian adv meaning 'together' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.

meanings.note: For emphasis.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

meanings.en: to guess, to work out, to think of
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'гадаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to guess, to realise', paired with 'догадываться'.

examples.trans: Why didn't I think of it at once!

examples.text: Какой глупый человек догадался это сделать?
examples.trans: What foolish person thought of doing that?

examples.text: Ты никогда сам не догадаешься об этом.
examples.trans: You will never guess this by yourself.

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective. Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('foolish, stupid').

examples.text: Эта дурацкая рыба — как плохой знак.
examples.trans: This foolish fish is like a bad sign.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.en: to do, to be engaged in
meanings.note: + instrumental: заниматься бизнесом = be in business

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be busy with, to do', paired with 'заняться'.

meanings.en: что ли = or what, I suppose
meanings.note: Colloquial tag. Core Russian part meaning 'whether, if; (что ли) or what' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

meanings.note: + instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'over, above; at' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.en: to begin, to start, to break out (intransitive)
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start, to break out', paired with 'начинаться'.

examples.trans: A fire started there! Fire engines and police are everywhere!

Мне неудобно = I feel awkward / bad about it
Impersonal predicate or adverb. Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'удобно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It is very uncomfortable to sit here.

examples.text: Мне жутко неудобно. Я не люблю быть в тягость.
examples.trans: I feel terribly awkward. I don't like being a burden.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

Surprise, fright or pain. Core Russian interj meaning 'oh' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We need to do everything and runs around on time.

examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to prepare without a reason.

meanings.note: Прямо так = just like that. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

рассказывай! = tell me (your news)!

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get ready, plan to, gather', paired with 'собираться'.

meanings.note: Colloquial, like здесь. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Please don't be angry with me.

examples.text: Поймите, была маленькая ошибка. Вы уж нас извините.
examples.trans: Understand, there was a small mistake. Please forgive us.
